label: CRA Product Conformity Assessment
description: Works out what a connected product must do to carry CE marking under the Cyber Resilience Act (EU) 2024/2847 by 11 December 2027: the product class (default, important class I or II, critical), the Annex I essential-requirements gap, the Annex VII technical-documentation outline, the Article 13(8) support-period determination, the Annex V declaration of conformity, and the Article 32 conformity route — including why an unlisted harmonised standard removes the self-assessment option for class I.

claudeKnowledge.description: Cyber Resilience Act (EU) 2024/2847 Arts. 2, 3, 6-8, 13, 27-32, 64, 69, 71 + Annexes I-VIII; Cybersecurity Act (EU) 2019/881 and the EUCC scheme (EU) 2024/482; Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 market surveillance; harmonised standards cited in the Official Journal; the Art. 7(4) implementing act on Annex III/IV technical descriptions; AI Act (EU) 2024/1689 Art. 12 interaction

guidedInputs.label: The product with digital elements
guidedInputs.description: What it is, what it does, what it connects to, what it protects, and who uses it. Include any remote data processing solution without which the product could not perform one of its functions — the Act treats that as part of the product (Art. 3(1) and 3(2)).
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. A rack-mounted network appliance running our own Linux-based firmware that performs stateful packet filtering and intrusion detection for small-business networks, managed through a cloud console we operate. Sold through EU distributors. Firmware is signed and updated over the air; the cloud console is required for configuration.

guidedInputs.label: Core functionality matching a listed category
guidedInputs.description: Classification turns on whether the product has the CORE FUNCTIONALITY of a category in Annex III (important, class I or II) or Annex IV (critical). Merely integrating such a product does not, by itself, make the integrating product important (Art. 7(1)). Select every category the product's own core functionality matches.

guidedInputs.label: Form of the product
guidedInputs.description: Drives how the CE marking is affixed (Art. 30(1)), whether Annex VII needs photographs and internal layout, and whether the free and open-source route in Art. 32(5) is available.

options.label: Hardware product with embedded software
A hardware or software component placed on the market separately
Standalone software

guidedInputs.label: Data connection
guidedInputs.description: Article 2(1) brings in products whose intended purpose or reasonably foreseeable use includes a direct or indirect logical or physical data connection to a device or network. This is the scope gate.

options.label: Direct network connection (internet, LAN, cellular)
Direct connection to another device (USB, Bluetooth, serial, proprietary radio)
Indirect only — reaches a network through another product

No data connection at all, in any foreseeable use

guidedInputs.label: Market status
guidedInputs.description: Article 69(2): products placed on the market before 11 December 2027 are caught only if substantially modified from that date. Article 69(3) derogates for Article 14 reporting, which reaches the whole installed base regardless.

options.label: In development — not yet placed on the market
Already on the market, no substantial modification planned

guidedInputs.label: Standards and certification position
guidedInputs.description: This decides the conformity route for class I products. Under Art. 32(2), a class I product only avoids third-party assessment where harmonised standards, common specifications or a certification scheme at assurance level at least 'substantial' have been applied IN FULL.

options.label: A harmonised standard cited in the OJ is applied in full
A harmonised standard is applied only in part
A Commission common specification under Art. 27(2) is applied
We hold a European cybersecurity certificate (e.g. EUCC) at assurance level 'substantial' or higher
Other standards applied (IEC 62443, ETSI EN 303 645, ISO/IEC 27001) but not cited under this Regulation
No standard applied, or none exists for these requirements
Do not know what has been cited in the Official Journal

guidedInputs.label: Years the product is expected to be in use
guidedInputs.description: Article 13(8): the support period must reflect how long the product is expected to be in use, and shall be AT LEAST five years unless the product is expected to be in use for less, in which case it matches the expected use time.

guidedInputs.label: Other Union legislation that applies
guidedInputs.description: Article 2 excludes some products entirely — Art. 2(2) for the three named regulations, Art. 2(3) for products certified under the civil aviation regulation, Art. 2(4) for marine equipment. Acts that do not exclude instead combine with the CRA under Articles 12 and 31(3), producing a single set of technical documentation and a single declaration of conformity.

guidedInputs.description: Most of Annex VII is documentation of things a competent engineering organisation already does. The gap is usually evidential, not technical.

guidedInputs.label: Size of the undertaking
guidedInputs.description: Article 33(5) lets microenterprises and small enterprises supply all Annex VII elements in a simplified format, using the form the Commission specifies by implementing act; notified bodies must accept it. Article 32(6) requires conformity-assessment fees to be reduced proportionately.

options.label: Microenterprise (<10 staff)

guidedInputs.label: Known concerns, contested classifications or commercial constraints
guidedInputs.description: Classification disputes, notified-body capacity worries, support-period commitments already made to customers, or requirements you believe do not apply.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. Sales have promised a three-year support window in contracts and we think the Act requires five. We cannot ship without a working default password because installers rely on it. We are not sure whether our appliance is a class II firewall or a class I router. We have no idea whether a harmonised standard exists for any of this and our distributor is asking for a declaration of conformity now.

exampleInput: We build a rack-mounted network security appliance for small businesses: our own Linux-based firmware doing stateful packet filtering and intrusion detection, managed through a cloud console we operate and which is required for configuration. Roughly 200 staff, sold through distributors in eight Member States, firmware signed and updated over the air. We currently ship with a documented default administrator password that installers rely on, we have architecture documentation but no formal cybersecurity risk assessment, no SBOM, no disclosure policy, and our standard contract promises three years of updates. A distributor has started asking for an EU declaration of conformity. Tell us: is this a class I or a class II important product, and what turns on that; what the Article 32 route actually is given we have applied IEC 62443 but nothing cited in the Official Journal; which Annex I requirements we currently fail and how badly; what Annex VII technical documentation we would have to produce and what we already have; what support period we must determine and whether our three-year contractual promise is a problem; and what the declaration of conformity has to say. We would also like to know what changes if we do nothing until 2027.
